hlst-01-c1.text: Marek Jankowiak (2017). The first Arab siege of Constantinople: The campaign of Yazid b. Mu'awiyah in 667-669. Byzantion'dan Constantinopolis'e Istanbul Kusatmalari (Istanbul Arastirmalari Enstitusu), pp. 201-228; University of Birmingham research portal.
hlst-01-c1.quote: rather than in 674-8, the first Arab attempt to conquer the Roman capital took place in 667-9 and was led by the son of the reigning caliph.
hlst-01-c1.claim: the historian Marek Jankowiak has argued that the main Arab attack came earlier, in 667 to 669

hlst-03-c3.text: M. Reibold, P. Paufler, A. A. Levin, W. Kochmann, N. Pätzke, D. C. Meyer (2006). Carbon nanotubes in an ancient Damascus sabre. Nature.
hlst-03-c3.quote: This microstructure may offer insight into the beautiful banding pattern of the ultrahigh-carbon steel created from an ancient recipe that was lost long ago.
hlst-03-c3.claim: The paper, "Carbon nanotubes in an ancient Damascus sabre," suggested the nanostructure might help explain the blade's banding.

hlst-04-c3.text: Joshua J. Mark (2023). Silphium. World History Encyclopedia.
hlst-04-c3.quote: Within the memory of the present generation, a single stalk is all that has ever been found there, and that was sent as a curiosity to the Emperor Nero.
hlst-04-c3.claim: and it was sent to the emperor Nero, who reigned from 54 to 68 CE, as a curiosity.
